entries.name: anydoc
entries.use_for: Convert Word, PowerPoint, Excel, OpenDocument, RTF, EPUB, CSV and PDF files to clean Markdown.
entries.why: One shared model and Markdown writer, so every format gives the same output style.
entries.summary: A fast Rust library that parses office documents and PDFs into one shared document model and writes GitHub-flavored Markdown. It has Node.js, Python and WebAssembly bindings. Format is detected from file contents, not the extension.
entries.best_for: Feeding office documents to LLMs as Markdown, locally and fast, including in the browser.
entries.not_for: Scanned pages. It cannot read them on its own and points to the hosted API with OCR.

entries.name: Apache DataFusion
entries.use_for: Embed a fast SQL and DataFrame query engine over Arrow data in your own system.
entries.why: Extensible Arrow-native query engine used as the core of many data products.
entries.summary: Apache DataFusion is an extensible query engine written in Rust, distributed as a crate, with SQL parsing and planning and Apache Parquet reading. You start from a working engine and customize it; optional Cargo features add nested, datetime, crypto, regex, unicode and compression support.
entries.best_for: Building domain-specific query engines, new database platforms, data pipelines or query languages in Rust on top of an embeddable SQL engine.
entries.not_for: A library for engine builders, not a ready-to-run database server or BI tool. Rust-centric; using it from other languages needs separate bindings.

entries.name: Apache Hamilton
entries.use_for: Define testable, modular data and ML pipelines as plain Python functions.
entries.why: Lightweight dataflow framework with built-in lineage, now an Apache project.
entries.summary: Lightweight Python library for building data transformation DAGs from plain functions: function parameters declare dependencies and the DAG is built automatically. Supports data validation, lineage, visualization and runs anywhere Python runs (scripts, notebooks, Airflow, FastAPI). Apache incubating project.
entries.best_for: Structuring feature engineering, data and ML pipelines as testable, modular, self-documenting Python functions with lineage.
entries.not_for: Large distributed orchestration or scheduling (it is a transformation framework, not a scheduler) or non-Python stacks. Still in Apache incubation.

entries.name: Burn
entries.use_for: Train and run deep learning models in Rust across CPU, CUDA, Metal and WebGPU
entries.why: Flexible Rust DL framework with swappable backends, autodiff and kernel fusion; 351 contributors.
entries.summary: Rust tensor library and deep learning framework with a single API over swappable backends (CPU, CUDA, Metal, WebGPU). Keeps PyTorch-like dynamic graphs while JIT-compiling tensor streams with automatic kernel fusion; the same code is used for training and inference.
entries.best_for: Training and deploying neural networks in Rust, on-device or browser inference, avoiding a Python-to-ONNX export step.
entries.not_for: Teams needing the broad model zoo and tutorials of PyTorch/Hugging Face. Smaller ecosystem and Rust learning curve.

entries.name: Chandra OCR 2
entries.use_for: Convert images and PDFs to Markdown, HTML or JSON with layout, tables, forms and handwriting.
entries.why: Handles handwriting, checkboxes, math and 90+ languages; runs locally or on vLLM.
entries.summary: An OCR model with a pip package and CLI. It turns documents into structured HTML, Markdown or JSON and keeps layout, extracts images and diagrams, and rebuilds forms. Inference runs through HuggingFace locally or a vLLM server.
entries.best_for: Document pipelines that need accurate layout, tables and handwriting without sending files to a cloud service.
entries.not_for: Competing with the vendor's API or larger companies. The weights use a modified OpenRAIL-M licence, free only for research, personal use and small startups.

entries.name: ChatLab
entries.use_for: Import chat exports from WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord and others and analyse them with SQL and AI on your machine.
entries.why: Keeps chats local and gives AI agents 24+ tools to search and summarise records.
entries.summary: An Electron and Vue desktop app, plus a CLI with a web UI and API. It parses exports from many chat apps into one model, stores them locally and lets you query with SQL and AI agents. Shared packages are used by both the app and CLI.
entries.best_for: Analysing your own chat history privately, or forking a local-first chat analysis tool.
entries.not_for: AGPL-3.0 licence. It works on exported chat files, not live accounts. Messenger and KakaoTalk are not yet supported.

entries.name: cuDF
entries.use_for: Run pandas-style dataframe operations on NVIDIA GPUs.
entries.why: RAPIDS GPU DataFrame library, with a drop-in pandas accelerator mode.
entries.summary: GPU-accelerated DataFrame library from NVIDIA RAPIDS. Includes libcudf (CUDA C++), pylibcudf, a pandas-like cudf API, cudf.pandas for zero-code-change acceleration of existing pandas code, a Polars GPU engine and a Dask backend.
entries.best_for: Speeding up pandas-style ETL and groupby/join workloads on large tabular data when you have an NVIDIA GPU.
entries.not_for: Machines without a CUDA-capable NVIDIA GPU, small datasets where transfer overhead dominates, or full pandas API parity guarantees.

entries.name: daily_stock_analysis
entries.use_for: Fork a self-run system that analyzes your stock watchlist with an LLM and pushes a daily report.
entries.why: Covers A-share, HK, US, JP, KR and TW markets and runs free on GitHub Actions or Docker.
entries.summary: An LLM-driven stock analysis app that pulls prices, news and fundamentals, writes a decision dashboard with scores and risk alerts, and sends it to WeCom, Feishu, Telegram, Discord, Slack or email. It has a web UI, an agent Q and A and a FastAPI service.
entries.best_for: You want a ready, hackable template for scheduled LLM market reports, especially for Chinese-market users.
entries.not_for: The README is mainly in Chinese. Free data sources are rate-limited and unreliable. Output is LLM analysis, not financial advice.

entries.name: Darts
entries.use_for: Forecast and detect anomalies in time series with classical and deep learning models.
entries.why: One unified API over statistical and neural forecasting models; Apache-2.0.
entries.summary: Python library for time series forecasting and anomaly detection with a scikit-learn-style fit()/predict() API across models from ARIMA to deep neural networks. Supports backtesting, ensembling, covariates, multivariate and probabilistic forecasts, and PyOD-based anomaly scoring.
entries.best_for: Time series forecasting where you want to compare statistical and neural models behind one API, with backtesting and probabilistic output.
entries.not_for: Streaming or real-time inference at scale, or tabular non-temporal ML. Deep models need PyTorch and extra dependencies.

entries.name: Debezium
entries.use_for: Stream row-level database changes (CDC) into Kafka or other sinks
entries.why: De facto open-source change data capture for Postgres, MySQL, MongoDB and more; 900+ contributors.
entries.summary: Open-source change data capture platform that streams row-level database changes (inserts, updates, deletes) from databases such as Postgres, MySQL and MongoDB to Kafka or other sinks. Builds and integration tests use Docker to start the source databases.
entries.best_for: Event streaming from existing databases, keeping caches/search indexes in sync, outbox pattern, replication to a data lake.
entries.not_for: Simple apps without Kafka-style infrastructure, or needing only periodic batch exports. Java/Kafka Connect-centric and operationally heavy.

entries.name: DeepAnalyze
entries.use_for: Run an open LLM agent that carries out data science tasks and writes analyst-style reports.
entries.why: Open model, training data, code and demo for an agentic LLM focused on data science.
entries.summary: An 8B agentic LLM that autonomously handles the data science pipeline: preparation, analysis, modeling, visualization and reporting. It works on structured, semi-structured and unstructured data and produces research reports. The model, code, training data and demo are released openly.
entries.best_for: Experimenting with autonomous data analysis, or building on an open data-science agent model.
entries.not_for: A research project. The model needs a GPU to host, and results should be checked by a person.

entries.name: DeepSpec
entries.use_for: Train and evaluate draft models for speculative decoding.
entries.why: Covers data prep, draft model code, training and benchmark evaluation in one repo.
entries.summary: A full-stack codebase for speculative decoding research. It has data preparation scripts, draft model implementations, training code and evaluation on benchmarks like GSM8K, MATH500 and HumanEval. Configs target models such as Qwen3-4B.
entries.best_for: Researchers and inference teams who want to train their own draft models.
entries.not_for: Heavy requirements: default setup assumes 8 GPUs, and the target cache can be about 38 TB.

entries.name: DeepSpeed
entries.use_for: Train and serve very large PyTorch models efficiently across many GPUs.
entries.why: ZeRO optimizations and parallelism used to train many large models; Apache-2.0.
entries.summary: DeepSpeed is a deep learning optimization library for PyTorch aimed at making large-scale training efficient. It provides system innovations including ZeRO, ZeRO-Infinity, 3D-Parallelism, Ulysses Sequence Parallelism and DeepSpeed-MoE, installs via pip, and compiles C++/CUDA/HIP extension ops.
entries.best_for: Training or serving very large models across many GPUs where memory partitioning, offloading and parallelism strategies are needed.
entries.not_for: Requires PyTorch installed first and a CUDA or ROCm compiler; tested mainly on NVIDIA and AMD datacenter GPUs. Some features (async IO, GDS) are unsupported on Windows. Overkill for small single-GPU models.

entries.name: DFlash
entries.use_for: Speed up LLM inference with a block diffusion draft model for speculative decoding.
entries.why: Ships draft checkpoints for many popular models and runs on Transformers, MLX, SGLang or vLLM.
entries.summary: DFlash is a lightweight block diffusion model used as a drafter for speculative decoding, so tokens are drafted in parallel. The repo has a CLI and backends for Transformers and Apple MLX, and checkpoints for Qwen, Gemma, Kimi, MiniMax and more.
entries.best_for: Researchers and serving engineers who want faster generation from supported open models.
entries.not_for: Only works for models that have a released draft checkpoint. Not a general inference server.

entries.name: fastai
entries.use_for: Train state-of-the-art deep learning models quickly with high-level PyTorch APIs.
entries.why: Proven high-level API with good defaults and a well-known course ecosystem.
entries.summary: High-level deep learning library on PyTorch with a layered architecture: fast defaults for vision, text, tabular and collaborative filtering, plus lower-level components (optimizer, callbacks, type dispatch) for researchers. Tied to the fast.ai course.
entries.best_for: Learning deep learning or quickly getting strong baselines on standard vision, text and tabular tasks with minimal code.
entries.not_for: Custom research needing full control and the latest architectures, or production serving stacks; PyTorch-based and less actively adopted than raw PyTorch/Hugging Face.

entries.name: Featuretools
entries.use_for: Automatically generate ML features from relational and temporal datasets.
entries.why: The best-known automated feature engineering library; BSD-3.
entries.summary: Python library for automated feature engineering. Deep Feature Synthesis (DFS) takes a multi-table EntitySet of related, timestamped dataframes and generates a feature matrix of aggregations and transformations for a target dataframe.
entries.best_for: Generating many candidate features from relational or temporal data (customers, sessions, transactions) before modeling.
entries.not_for: Single flat tables or deep learning on unstructured data. Can generate very large feature sets needing selection.

entries.name: ggml
entries.use_for: Build lightweight on-device ML inference with quantized tensors
entries.why: The tensor library behind llama.cpp and whisper.cpp; no dependencies and broad hardware support.
entries.summary: Plain C/C++ tensor library for machine learning with no dependencies. Provides integer quantization (2-8 bit plus MXFP4/NVFP4), SIMD kernels, and CPU, GPU and WebAssembly backends. It underlies llama.cpp and whisper.cpp and defines the GGUF file format.
entries.best_for: Embedding lightweight on-device inference, running quantized models on CPU or edge hardware, building llama.cpp-style engines.
entries.not_for: Model training or high-level APIs. Low-level library; for ready-made LLM running use llama.cpp.

entries.name: GLM-OCR
entries.use_for: Extract text, tables and formulas from complex documents with a small multimodal OCR model.
entries.why: Reports the top score on OmniDocBench V1.5 with a 0.5B language decoder.
entries.summary: A multimodal OCR model built on the GLM-V encoder-decoder design. It runs layout analysis, then recognises regions in parallel. You can use the hosted Zhipu API with no GPU, or run the model yourself.
entries.best_for: Document parsing for invoices, tables, code-heavy pages and seals where plain OCR struggles.
entries.not_for: The hosted route needs a Zhipu API key. Benchmark claims come from the authors.

entries.name: GR00T Whole-Body Control
entries.use_for: Train, test and deploy whole-body controllers and motion models for humanoid robots.
entries.why: Includes the controllers behind GR00T N1.5/N1.6, the GEAR-SONIC series and MotionBricks.
entries.summary: NVIDIA's codebase with model checkpoints and scripts for humanoid controllers. It has a Python training stack and a C++ inference stack for deploying SONIC policies on real hardware.
entries.best_for: Humanoid robotics teams that use Isaac Lab and want a working whole-body control baseline.
entries.not_for: Needs NVIDIA simulation and robot hardware. The license is not clearly stated, so read it before commercial use.

entries.name: Gradio
entries.use_for: Wrap an ML model in a shareable web UI or API in a few lines of Python
entries.why: Standard for ML demos and Hugging Face Spaces; auto-generates API endpoints and client libraries.
entries.summary: Python package for turning an ML model, API or any Python function into a web UI in a few lines (Interface, Blocks). Provides sharing links, auto-generated API endpoints and client libraries, and runs in notebooks, Colab or standalone.
entries.best_for: Quick ML demos, internal tools and Hugging Face Spaces without writing JavaScript or CSS.
entries.not_for: Polished, custom-branded production web apps or complex multi-page apps; it is demo/tool oriented.

entries.name: Heretic
entries.use_for: Automatically remove refusal behavior from transformer language models with directional ablation.
entries.why: Tunes abliteration parameters with Optuna to cut refusals while keeping the model close to the original.
entries.summary: Heretic removes safety alignment from transformer LLMs without post-training. It combines directional ablation with a TPE optimizer that minimizes refusals and KL divergence from the original model. You run one command on a model name. It supports most dense and several MoE models.
entries.best_for: Researchers and hobbyists who want an uncensored variant of an open model without hand-tuning.
entries.not_for: Pure state-space models and some research architectures are not supported. Removes safety behavior, so check use and model license. AGPL-3.0.

entries.name: JupyterLab
entries.use_for: Notebook-based environment for interactive data science, extensible with plugins
entries.why: The standard notebook interface for data work, with a large extension ecosystem
entries.summary: Web-based interactive computing environment built on the Jupyter Notebook: notebooks, terminal, text editor, file browser and rich outputs in a flexible layout. Extensible through npm-based extensions, distributed via PyPI or conda.
entries.best_for: Exploratory data science, teaching and reproducible research in notebooks, with a large extension ecosystem.
entries.not_for: Production pipelines or clean version control of notebooks (JSON diffs, hidden state). Consider marimo for reactive, git-friendly notebooks.

entries.name: Kedro
entries.use_for: Structure data science code into reproducible, testable pipelines
entries.why: LF AI & Data project bringing software engineering practice (data catalog, modular pipelines) to DS projects.
entries.summary: Python framework for production-ready data engineering and data science pipelines. Provides a project template, a Data Catalog of connectors across file formats and storage, modular pipelines and pipeline visualization, applying software engineering practices. Hosted by LF AI & Data.
entries.best_for: Structuring reproducible, maintainable ML/data projects in teams, moving notebook code into modular pipelines.
entries.not_for: Quick one-off analysis, or workflow scheduling (it is not an orchestrator; pair with Airflow or similar). Imposes project conventions.

entries.name: Kev
entries.use_for: Train and serve small models that answer yes/no, multiple-choice and rating questions about text.
entries.why: Calibrated probabilities and an API matching TypeSafe's System One.
entries.summary: A family of small decision models (0.8B to 27B) built on Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.8 as LoRA adapters with a pointer head. Several questions are answered in one request. It runs on CUDA and Apple Silicon, handles up to 65,536 tokens, and can be fine-tuned and deployed with one command.
entries.best_for: Fast, cheap classification and routing decisions you can run yourself.
entries.not_for: Hard knowledge questions. The README shows Kev-27B trails Jev on MMLU-Pro, and small models struggle with date arithmetic.

entries.name: Kimodo
entries.use_for: Generate 3D human and robot motion from text prompts and kinematic constraints.
entries.why: Trained on 700 hours of commercially-friendly mocap, with keyframe and path controls.
entries.summary: A kinematic motion diffusion model with inference code and a CLI for human and robot skeletons. It adds an interactive timeline demo for authoring motion, a benchmark on BONES-SEED, and text annotations.
entries.best_for: Animation and robotics teams who need text-controlled motion generation with pose and path constraints.
entries.not_for: Needs a GPU and model downloads. Research-grade code, not a game-engine plugin.

entries.name: LeWorldModel (LeWM)
entries.use_for: Train and evaluate a JEPA world model from raw pixels.
entries.why: Official code for a JEPA that trains end to end with only two loss terms.
entries.summary: Research code for LeWorldModel, a joint-embedding predictive architecture that learns from pixels. The PyTorch model sits in jepa.py, with Hydra configs, HDF5 datasets and planning evaluation built on stable-worldmodel and stable-pretraining.
entries.best_for: Researchers reproducing the paper or studying a simple, stable JEPA training setup.
entries.not_for: Paper-companion code, not a packaged library. Expects specific datasets, WandB setup and the stable-worldmodel stack.

entries.name: LingBot-Map
entries.use_for: Reconstruct 3D scenes from streaming video or image folders with a geometric context transformer.
entries.why: Handles very long sequences using windowed inference, with an interactive viewer.
entries.summary: Research code and weights for streaming 3D reconstruction. A demo script loads images or a video and opens an interactive viser viewer. For long sequences it uses sliding-window inference and an offline rendering pipeline.
entries.best_for: Researchers and engineers testing 3D reconstruction from video, such as indoor walkthroughs or driving scenes.
entries.not_for: Plug-and-play production use. It needs a GPU and a downloaded model checkpoint, and is paper-style research code.

entries.name: LiteParse
entries.use_for: Parse PDFs locally into Markdown, JSON or text with bounding boxes, for LLM and RAG pipelines.
entries.why: About 2 to 5ms per page, fully local, usable from Rust, Node, Python and the browser.
entries.summary: A fast local PDF parser using PDFium with built-in Tesseract OCR or any HTTP OCR server. It outputs structured Markdown, JSON or text, makes page screenshots, and can check whether a document needs heavier parsing.
entries.best_for: Quick, private document ingestion where speed matters more than perfect layout.
entries.not_for: Dense tables, multi-column layouts, charts or scans. The README points those to the paid LlamaParse cloud service.

entries.name: marimo
entries.use_for: Reactive Python notebooks stored as plain .py files, runnable as scripts or deployable as apps
entries.why: Fixes Jupyter hidden-state and git-diff pain: reactive execution, pure Python files, built-in UI elements
entries.summary: Reactive Python notebook where running a cell or changing a UI element reruns dependent cells automatically. Notebooks are stored as plain .py files (with SQL support), runnable as scripts and deployable as apps; positioned as replacing Jupyter, Streamlit and papermill.
entries.best_for: Reproducible, git-friendly notebooks and quick data apps in Python without hidden state.
entries.not_for: Teams tied to .ipynb workflows and Jupyter extensions, or R/Julia kernels. Reactive execution model differs from Jupyter.

entries.name: Matplotlib
entries.use_for: The foundational Python plotting library for static, animated and interactive figures
entries.why: Underpins seaborn, pandas plotting and most of the scientific Python stack; the default for publication-quality figures

license_verified.note: Matplotlib License (PSF-derived permissive); PyPI classifier OSI Approved :: Python Software Foundation License

entries.summary: Foundational Python plotting library for static, animated and interactive figures. Produces publication-quality output in many formats and works in scripts, IPython, web servers and GUI toolkits; underlies many higher-level plotting libraries.
entries.best_for: Publication-quality static charts and full control over figure details in Python and scientific workflows.
entries.not_for: Interactive web dashboards or quick attractive defaults (use Plotly, Altair or seaborn). API is verbose.

entries.name: MLflow
entries.use_for: Track experiments, package models, manage a model registry and evaluate LLM apps
entries.why: The most widely used open MLOps platform for experiment tracking and model lifecycle management
entries.summary: Open-source platform for the AI/ML lifecycle: experiment tracking, model packaging and registry, plus LLM and agent observability, evaluation, prompt management and an AI Gateway. Works with many ML and GenAI frameworks.
entries.best_for: Tracking experiments, versioning models and monitoring or evaluating LLM apps, from solo use to team servers.
entries.not_for: Pure workflow orchestration or feature stores. Self-hosted tracking server needs setup and backing storage.

entries.name: nanochat
entries.use_for: Train and chat with your own small GPT-style LLM end to end on one GPU node.
entries.why: Minimal, hackable code covering tokenization, pretraining, finetuning, evaluation and inference.
entries.summary: nanochat is a simple experimental harness for training LLMs on a single GPU node. One depth setting configures a whole series of compute-optimal models. A speedrun script trains a GPT-2-grade model in about 2 hours on 8 H100s, then you chat with it over a CLI.
entries.best_for: You want to learn or experiment with the full LLM training pipeline in small, readable code.
entries.not_for: It trains small models for research and learning, not frontier-quality assistants, and needs rented GPUs for a real run.

entries.name: NumPy
entries.use_for: N-dimensional arrays and fast numerical computing for Python
entries.why: The base array library that pandas, scikit-learn, PyTorch interop and nearly all scientific Python builds on

license_verified.note: LICENSE.txt is BSD 3-clause; bundled components under compatible licenses

entries.summary: Fundamental Python package for scientific computing: N-dimensional array object, broadcasting functions, linear algebra, Fourier transform and random number tools, and C/C++/Fortran integration. The base of the scientific Python stack.
entries.best_for: Any numeric or array computing in Python, and the foundation for pandas, SciPy and scikit-learn.
entries.not_for: GPU or autodiff workloads (use PyTorch/JAX/CuPy), or labeled tabular data (use pandas/Polars).

entries.name: OpenMed
entries.use_for: Extract medical entities and de-identify PII in clinical text on hardware you control.
entries.why: Large model catalog with Python, Apple MLX, Android and browser runtimes under an Apache-2.0 SDK.
entries.summary: OpenMed is a local-first SDK for clinical text. It runs NER models for diseases and other entities, and PII detection and de-identification in 35 languages. The core runtime works locally once model files are downloaded.
entries.best_for: Health-tech teams that need on-device or self-hosted clinical NER and de-identification.
entries.not_for: Using the SDK does not make you HIPAA compliant, and model and dataset licenses vary. Validate for your clinical use.

entries.name: pandas
entries.use_for: Load, clean, transform and analyze tabular data with DataFrames in Python.
entries.why: The standard Python dataframe library with the largest ecosystem of integrations.
entries.summary: Python package providing labeled data structures (Series, DataFrame) for loading, cleaning, transforming and analyzing tabular data. It is the standard high-level building block for data analysis in Python with the widest ecosystem of integrations.
entries.best_for: Everyday data wrangling, analysis and I/O (CSV, Excel, SQL, Parquet) on datasets that fit in memory.
entries.not_for: Larger-than-memory or very large datasets and maximum speed (consider Polars or DuckDB); memory-heavy.

entries.name: pdf-inspector
entries.use_for: Tell scanned PDFs from text PDFs and extract text and Markdown from the text ones without OCR.
entries.why: Classifies a PDF in tens of milliseconds so only the pages that need OCR get sent to it.
entries.summary: A fast Rust library that classifies PDFs as text-based, scanned, image-based or mixed. For text PDFs it extracts text with position and converts to Markdown, with table, multi-column and CID font handling. It has Python, Node.js and WebAssembly bindings.
entries.best_for: PDF pipelines that want to skip costly OCR for the many PDFs that already hold text.
entries.not_for: Scanned documents on their own; OCR is optional and only for native Rust and CLI use.

entries.name: Polars
entries.use_for: Process large tabular datasets fast with a lazy, multi-threaded DataFrame engine.
entries.why: Rust-based, much faster than pandas on many workloads, with Python, Rust and Node APIs.
entries.summary: Analytical query engine for DataFrames written in Rust, with multi-threaded vectorized execution, lazy and eager modes with query optimization, a streaming engine for larger-than-RAM data and an expression API. Has Python, Rust, Node.js and R bindings.
entries.best_for: Fast processing of large tabular datasets and ETL where pandas is too slow or memory hungry.
entries.not_for: Code deeply tied to pandas APIs or libraries expecting pandas objects; different API requires rewriting.

entries.name: Prediction Market Analysis
entries.use_for: Collect and analyze Polymarket and Kalshi market and trade data with a ready dataset.
entries.why: Ships indexers, parquet storage and extensible analysis scripts plus a large public dataset.
entries.summary: A framework for analyzing prediction market data. It includes pre-collected Polymarket and Kalshi datasets, indexers for market metadata and trade history via API and blockchain, parquet storage with resumable progress, and analysis scripts that produce figures and statistics. Run with make index and make analyze.
entries.best_for: You research prediction markets and want a starting dataset and scripts to extend.
entries.not_for: A research toolkit, not a trading bot. Covers Polymarket and Kalshi only.

entries.name: PyGWalker
entries.use_for: Explore a DataFrame with a Tableau-style drag-and-drop UI inside Jupyter
entries.why: Turns pandas/polars DataFrames into an interactive visual analysis UI in notebooks and Streamlit.
entries.summary: Python library that turns a pandas or polars DataFrame into a Tableau-style drag-and-drop visual exploration UI inside Jupyter, with Streamlit and other app integrations.
entries.best_for: Quick interactive exploratory data analysis and chart building in notebooks without writing plotting code.
entries.not_for: Publication-ready custom charts, scripted/reproducible plots, or large-scale BI dashboards.

entries.name: PyOD
entries.use_for: Detect anomalies and outliers in tabular, time series or other data
entries.why: 60+ detectors behind a scikit-learn-style API; the go-to Python anomaly detection library.
entries.summary: PyOD is a Python library for outlier and anomaly detection with 61 detectors across tabular, time series, graph, text, image and audio data behind one fit/predict API. PyOD 3 adds ADEngine to choose, compare and assess detectors automatically, plus an od-expert agent skill and an optional MCP server.
entries.best_for: Detecting anomalies or outliers in Python data with many interchangeable algorithms, or letting an AI agent run anomaly-detection investigations.
entries.not_for: Focused on anomaly detection only, not general ML. The agentic and MCP layers need extra installs; a Python library rather than a hosted monitoring service.

entries.name: PyTorch
entries.use_for: Build and train neural networks with tensors, autograd and GPU acceleration.
entries.why: The dominant deep learning framework in research and production; BSD-style license (verified).
entries.summary: Python deep learning framework providing NumPy-like tensor computation with GPU acceleration and tape-based autograd for dynamic neural networks. Python-first, extensible with NumPy/SciPy/Cython, widely used in research and production.
entries.best_for: Building and training custom neural networks, research, and most modern deep learning and LLM work.
entries.not_for: Classical tabular ML (use scikit-learn/XGBoost) or tiny edge targets. Large install, and low-level training loops are manual.

entries.name: Ray
entries.use_for: Scale Python and ML workloads across clusters: distributed training, tuning, data and serving
entries.why: Standard compute engine for scaling ML from a laptop to a cluster; powers training and inference at many large labs
entries.summary: Distributed compute framework for scaling Python and ML workloads across clusters, with libraries for distributed training, hyperparameter tuning, data processing, reinforcement learning and model serving.
entries.best_for: Scaling Python or ML jobs from a laptop to a cluster: distributed training, tuning, batch inference, serving.
entries.not_for: Single-machine workloads where multiprocessing or Dask suffice; cluster operations add complexity.

entries.name: scikit-learn
entries.use_for: Train and evaluate classical ML models: classification, regression, clustering and preprocessing.
entries.why: The default library for classical ML in Python, with a consistent, well-documented API.
entries.summary: scikit-learn is a Python module for machine learning built on top of SciPy and distributed under the 3-Clause BSD license. It depends on NumPy, SciPy, joblib and threadpoolctl, installs via pip or conda, and offers plotting helpers when Matplotlib is available.
entries.best_for: Classical machine learning in Python: classification, regression, clustering, preprocessing and model evaluation on tabular data.
entries.not_for: Not a deep learning framework; no GPU-centric neural network training. Python only.

entries.name: Soup
entries.use_for: Fine-tune and post-train LLMs from one YAML config and one command, even on small GPUs.
entries.why: Layer streaming trains an 8B model in about 3 GB of VRAM (still beta).
entries.summary: A CLI that fine-tunes LLMs from a YAML file with soup train. It picks batch size, detects GPUs and handles quantization such as QLoRA. Opt-in layer streaming feeds one decoder layer at a time to the GPU so large models fit on a 4 GB laptop card.
entries.best_for: Fine-tuning on your own GPU without writing training scripts.
entries.not_for: Stable pipelines. Layer streaming is beta, and v0.76 now refuses settings that were never applied, so old configs may stop loading.

entries.name: StarVLA
entries.use_for: Build and compare vision-language-action models for robots with swappable parts.
entries.why: Backbones and action heads are decoupled, so a new variant is mostly a swap.
entries.summary: A research codebase for vision-language-action robot models. Model, data, trainer, config and evaluation are separate parts. It ships action-head variants (FAST, OFT, flow-matching PI, GR00T-style) that share one data interface.
entries.best_for: Robotics researchers who want to prototype and benchmark VLA models quickly.
entries.not_for: A research platform, not a production robot stack. The license is not clearly stated, so check it before reuse.

entries.name: TensorFlow.js
entries.use_for: Train and run ML models in the browser or Node.js with WebGL/WebGPU acceleration.
entries.why: The most established ML library for JavaScript, with prebuilt models and converters.
entries.summary: JavaScript library for training and deploying ML models in the browser or Node.js with WebGL/WebGPU acceleration. Offers a low-level linear algebra API and a high-level layers API, model converters for existing TensorFlow models, and retraining.
entries.best_for: Running or fine-tuning ML models client-side in browsers or Node.js, using pretrained models and converters.
entries.not_for: Large-scale training or cutting-edge LLMs; better served by Python frameworks or ONNX/transformers.js runtimes.

entries.name: Transformers
entries.use_for: Load, fine-tune and run pretrained models for text, vision, audio and multimodal tasks
entries.why: The de-facto model-definition library: thousands of architectures and direct access to the Hugging Face Hub
entries.summary: Model-definition library for pretrained text, vision, audio, video and multimodal models, supporting inference and training. Central model definitions are compatible with training frameworks and inference engines (vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, etc.) and the Hugging Face Hub.
entries.best_for: Loading, fine-tuning and running pretrained models for NLP, vision, audio and LLMs with the Hugging Face ecosystem.
entries.not_for: Lean production serving (use vLLM/TGI/ONNX) or tabular ML. Heavy dependencies and large model downloads.

entries.name: XGBoost
entries.use_for: Scalable gradient-boosted trees for tabular classification, regression and ranking
entries.why: Still the strongest default for tabular data; GPU and distributed training, scikit-learn compatible API
entries.summary: Optimized gradient boosting library implementing parallel tree boosting (GBDT/GBM). Runs on Kubernetes, Hadoop, Spark, Dask and GPUs, scales beyond billions of examples, with a scikit-learn-compatible API.
entries.best_for: Tabular classification, regression and ranking where gradient boosting is the strong default, including distributed or GPU training.
entries.not_for: Unstructured data like images, text or audio (use deep learning), or extrapolating time trends.

entries.name: XQuad
entries.use_for: Write a QUBO, Ising or integer optimization problem once and run it on quantum or classical solvers.
entries.why: A shared virtual machine and spec, so one problem can be retargeted to any supported backend.
entries.summary: XQuad is a toolchain for quadratic optimization problems. It has Rust crates and Python packages built around one VM spec, with the Rust and Python VMs checked against each other in CI. Includes TSP and maxcut examples.
entries.best_for: Researchers and developers who want a backend-neutral way to express quadratic optimization and switch between annealers and classical solvers.
entries.not_for: Production use: the README says the instruction set, binary format and API may change before v1.0. AGPL-3.0 licence.

entries.name: ydata-profiling
entries.use_for: Generate a full EDA and data-quality report from a DataFrame in one line
entries.why: Formerly pandas-profiling; HTML reports with correlations, missing values and alerts for Pandas and Spark.
entries.summary: Renamed successor of ydata-profiling (pandas-profiling). Generates an extended one-line exploratory data analysis report from a DataFrame, with HTML reports covering correlations, missing values, distributions and data quality alerts; supports pandas and Spark.
entries.best_for: Quick automated EDA and data-quality checks at the start of a data project.
entries.not_for: Deep custom analysis or very large data (reports are slow on wide/huge frames). Old ydata-profiling package no longer receives updates.
